newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON STAY ON COURSE FOR CUP DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON STAY ON COURSE FOR CUP DOUBLE.

text.p: Late goals from Robbie Earle and Dean Holdsworth gave Wimbledon a 2-0 quarter-final victory at Sheffield Wednesday on Sunday to put the London club into the English F.A. Cup semifinals for only the second time.

Wimbledon last reached the semifinals in 1988 when they won the trophy and the victory meant they are still closing in on two cups this season. On Tuesday, they play Leicester in the second leg of the League Cup semifinal after drawing the away leg 0-0.
Earle's 75th minute goal maintained his record of scoring in every round and came from a move engineered by Neil Ardley who played the ball deep into the Wednesday area.
Marcus Gayle had time to tee Earle up for his shot and he blasted it high into the roof of the net from close range.

Holdsworth put the finishing touches to the victory in the last minute soon after coming on as a substitute. He collected the ball in space from Norwegian Oyvind Leonhardsen who was allowed to break free after a mistake by Ian Nolan.
Leonhardsen crossed to Holdsworth who slotted the ball past goalkeeper Kevin Pressman.
Wednesday wasted three clear chances to score earlier in the second half and only had themselves to blame for losing for only the second time in 23 matches.
Wimbledon now meet south London neighbours Chelsea in one semifinal. Middlesbrough face Chesterfield in the other and neither club has reached the last four previously.
